styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Salsa schools, street murals and the city's music scene.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Market lunches, pandebono and Pacific-coast cooking.

styles.label: Nature
styles.blurb: Cloud forest, birdwatching and Andean day walks.

stays.why: Leafy, walkable and full of restaurants and cafés. Good base for first-time visitors.
Quiet, central and close to the river; a short taxi ride to Granada and San Antonio.
Colonial hilltop lanes with cafés and sunset views. Charming but hilly; take taxis after dark.
Cheapest and most historic, near the gold museum and markets. Busy and rough-edged at night.

food: Try local snacks: pandebono (cheese bread), aborrajados (fried plantain with cheese) and cholado, a fruit-and-ice cup.
Lunch at a market or a set-menu 'corrientazo' spot: soup, rice, beans and meat for a low price. Check the day's price on the board.
Look for Pacific-coast cooking: fish and shellfish in coconut sauce, plus fried plantain. Ask what is fresh that day.
Granada and San Antonio have the widest choice of cafés and restaurants; book ahead on weekend evenings.
Coffee is excellent. Order tinto (black) or a latte at a local café rather than a chain.
more_time: Salsa fans: swap a sightseeing afternoon for a beginner dance class in Granada. Prices vary; book a day ahead.
Birdwatchers: a guided early-morning trip to a nearby cloud-forest reserve is worth a half day. Check conditions on the day.
History buffs: add a half day for the gold museum and the colonial churches in Centro, with a taxi back before dark.

recommend.why: Three nights lets you see the sights, take a salsa class and fit in one nature day trip without rushing.

month_notes: January: warm days around 25°C and cool nights near 18°C. Expect rain on many days; carry a light rain jacket.
February: similar to January, slightly warmer nights. Rain is common, so keep indoor plans ready.
March: one of the wettest months, with rain on most days. Plan outdoor trips for the morning.
April: still very wet. Short heavy showers are likely; waterproof shoes help.
May: rain on many days but often in bursts. Good month for salsa and food indoors.
June: slightly drier than May. Mild days around 25°C; evenings comfortable.
July: one of the drier months, with rain on fewer days. Good for outdoor plans.
August: like July, relatively dry and mild. A solid month for nature day trips.
September: the warmest highs, around 27°C. Rain is still common; start early.
October: one of the wettest months. Expect rain most days; keep plans flexible.
November: very wet again. Indoor culture and food plans work best.
December: wet but festive. Mild days around 25°C; pack a rain layer.

climate_guide.summary: Cali is mild all year, around 25°C by day and 18–19°C at night. Rain is common in every month, so plan around showers.

items.title: Mild all year
items.text: Highs stay near 25–27°C and lows near 18–19°C. No extreme heat or cold; light layers work.

items.title: Rain in every month
items.text: Expect rain on 22–28 days a month. Showers are often short; carry a compact rain jacket.

items.title: Wettest months: March, October, November
items.text: Rain on about 27–28 days. Keep indoor options and a taxi budget ready.

items.title: Drier months: February, July, August
items.text: Rain on about 22 days. Still pack rain gear, but outdoor plans are easier.

items.title: Plan mornings outdoors
items.text: Rain often builds later in the day. Do nature trips and walking early, then move indoors.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light clothes, a rain jacket or umbrella, and comfortable shoes for hilly, wet streets. A light layer for cool evenings.

transit.best: Taxis and ride apps for most trips; MIO buses if you're saving money.

modes.text: No metro or train in the city. Don't plan around rail.

MIO buses run in exclusive lanes with air-conditioned cars and smart-card payment. The MIO card costs about COP$6,000; a single ride is about COP$3,500. About 23 other urban bus companies also cover the city, about COP$3,500 a trip.
Taxis are fast and affordable; call one and check the meter is running. Uber and DiDi operate in Cali; use official taxis at night.
Possible, but city traffic and parking are a hassle. Better for out-of-town day trips; check licence rules.
Walking works in Granada and San Antonio. Use taxis after dark.
